{{short description|Cocycle in an entire cyclic cohomology group}}
{{no footnotes|date=November 2018}}
In [[noncommutative geometry]], the '''Jaffe–Lesniewski–Osterwalder''' ('''JLO''') '''cocycle''' (named after [[Arthur Jaffe]], Andrzej Lesniewski, and [[Konrad Osterwalder]]) is a [[Group cohomology|cocycle]] in an entire [[cyclic cohomology]] group. It is a non-commutative version of the classic [[Chern character]] of the conventional [[differential geometry]]. In noncommutative geometry, the concept of a manifold is replaced by a noncommutative algebra <math>\mathcal{A}</math> of "functions" on the putative noncommutative space. The cyclic cohomology of the algebra <math>\mathcal{A}</math> contains the information about the topology of that noncommutative space, very much as the [[de Rham cohomology]] contains the information about the topology of a conventional manifold.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last=Jaffe |first=Arthur |title=Quantum Harmonic Analysis and Geometric Invariants |date=1997-09-08 |eprint=physics/9709011 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Higson |first=Nigel |url=http://www.math.psu.edu/higson/Slides/trieste4.pdf |title=K-Theory and Noncommutative Geometry |date=2002 |publisher=Penn State University |pages=Lecture 4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100624222022/http://www.math.psu.edu/higson/Slides/trieste4.pdf |archive-date=2010-06-24 }}</ref>

The JLO cocycle is associated with a metric structure of non-commutative differential geometry known as a <math>\theta</math>-summable [[spectral triple]] (also known as a <math>\theta</math>-summable Fredholm module). It was first introduced in a 1988 paper by Jaffe, Lesniewski, and Osterwalder.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jaffe |first1=Arthur |last2=Lesniewski |first2=Andrzej |last3=Osterwalder |first3=Konrad |date=1988 |title=Quantum $K$-theory. I. The Chern character |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-118/issue-1/Quantum-K-theory-I-The-Chern-character/cmp/1104161905.full |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=118 |issue=1 |pages=1–14 |doi=10.1007/BF01218474 |bibcode=1988CMaPh.118....1J |issn=0010-3616|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== <math>\theta</math>-summable spectral triples ==

The input to the JLO construction is a ''<math>\theta</math>-summable spectral triple.'' These triples consists of the following data:

(a) A [[Hilbert space]] <math>\mathcal{H}</math> such that <math>\mathcal{A}</math> acts on it as an algebra of bounded operators.

(b) A <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math>-grading <math>\gamma</math> on <math>\mathcal{H}</math>, <math>\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_0\oplus\mathcal{H}_1</math>. We assume that the algebra <math>\mathcal{A}</math> is even under the <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math>-grading, i.e. <math>a\gamma=\gamma a</math>, for all <math>a\in\mathcal{A}</math>.

(c) A self-adjoint (unbounded) operator <math>D</math>, called the ''Dirac operator'' such that

:(i) <math>D</math> is odd under <math>\gamma</math>, i.e. <math>D\gamma=-\gamma D</math>.

:(ii) Each <math>a\in\mathcal{A}</math> maps the domain of <math>D</math>, <math>\mathrm{Dom}\left(D\right)</math> into itself, and the operator <math>\left[D,a\right]:\mathrm{Dom}\left(D\right)\to\mathcal{H}</math> is bounded.

:(iii) <math>\mathrm{tr}\left(e^{-tD^2}\right)<\infty</math>, for all <math>t>0</math>.

A classic example of a <math>\theta</math>-summable spectral triple arises as follows. Let <math>M</math> be a compact [[spin manifold]], <math>\mathcal{A}=C^\infty\left(M\right)</math>, the algebra of smooth functions on <math>M</math>, <math>\mathcal{H}</math> the Hilbert space of square integrable forms on <math>M</math>, and <math>D</math> the standard Dirac operator.

== The cocycle ==

Given a <math>\theta</math>-summable spectral triple, the JLO cocycle <math>\Phi_t\left(D\right)</math> associated to the triple is a sequence

:<math>\Phi_t\left(D\right)=\left(\Phi_t^0\left(D\right),\Phi_t^2\left(D\right),\Phi_t^4\left(D\right),\ldots\right)</math>

of functionals on the algebra <math>\mathcal{A}</math>, where

:<math>\Phi_t^0\left(D\right)\left(a_0\right)=\mathrm{tr}\left(\gamma a_0 e^{-tD^2}\right),</math>
:<math>\Phi_t^n\left(D\right)\left(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n\right)=\int_{0\leq s_1\leq\ldots s_n\leq t}\mathrm{tr}\left(\gamma a_0 e^{-s_1 D^2}\left[D,a_1\right]e^{-\left(s_2-s_1\right)D^2}\ldots\left[D,a_n\right]e^{-\left(t-s_n\right)D^2}\right)ds_1\ldots ds_n,</math>

for <math>n=2,4,\dots</math>. The cohomology class defined by <math>\Phi_t\left(D\right)</math> is independent of the value of <math>t</math>
